children: There could come a moment of acute discomfort for Australia money markets on Wednesday if inflation data for October delivers a higher-than-expected shock. Headline inflation is expected to rise to an uncomfortable 4.7%, but the more important trimmed mean measure is forecast to be little changed, landing at around 3.6% year over year. With recent economic data coming in weak, markets are already starting to price in interest-rate cuts next year, so an upward inflation shock would trigger volatility. Reserve Bank of Australia Gov. Michele Bullock said last week inflation risks remain skewed toward a rise. Central bank rhetoric remains hawkish generally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
